conventions.convention: The interpolation index n denotes n+1 strictly increasing real nodes x_0<⋯<x_n; n=0 is admissible. Products omitting index j follow the explicitly defined increasing omitted-node list. Empty products equal 1.

Formal polynomials are canonical coefficient lists with nonzero final coefficient, together with a separate zero object. The zero polynomial has no degree. Zero padding describes evaluation vectors without changing formal objects.
Natural numbers used as real scalars denote their canonical real images; the real factorial is the product of those images and agrees with the image of the natural factorial.

The remainder theorem assumes a<b and f∈C^{n+1}([a,b]), including continuous one-sided endpoint derivatives. At a node the error is zero; otherwise ξ lies strictly between the extreme points of the nodes together with the query.
Barycentric quotients are used only away from nodes. Exact node queries return the prescribed nodal value separately.

Checked arithmetic rejects division by zero and nonzero exact results outside the normal range before rounding. Successful rounding returns an element of the supplied finite floating-point set. Success carries no accuracy or conditioning guarantee.
The equispaced growth witness uses 2m+1 nodes and m≥6. Its unit-bounded nodal data vary with m; it makes no divergence assertion for a single fixed continuous function.

load_bearing.statement: For n∈ℕ, increasing real nodes x_0<⋯<x_n, and real data, each cardinal function ℓ_j is the evaluation of a formal polynomial of degree n; ω_n is the evaluation of a monic formal polynomial of degree n+1 and is nonzero off the nodes; I_n y is the evaluation of a formal polynomial of degree at most n; ℓ_j(x_i) is 1 for i=j and 0 otherwise.
For n∈ℕ, n≥0, distinct increasing real nodes x_0<⋯<x_n, and real data y_0,…,y_n, I_n y is the unique real polynomial of degree at most n satisfying p(x_i)=y_i for every i=0,…,n.
For n+1 increasing distinct real nodes, define ω_n(X)=∏_{k=0}^n(X−x_k), w_j=(∏_{k≠j}(x_j−x_k))^{-1}, ℓ_j(X)=∏_{k≠j}(X−x_k)/(x_j−x_k), and I_n y(X)=∑_{j=0}^n y_jℓ_j(X).

For n≥0, a<b, increasing nodes in [a,b], f∈C^{n+1}([a,b],ℝ), and p=I_n f, node queries have zero error. For every non-node x∈[a,b], some ξ∈(min{x,x_0},max{x,x_n}) satisfies f(x)−p(x)=f^{(n+1)}(ξ)ω_n(x)/(n+1)!_ℝ.

For increasing distinct real nodes and real data, every non-node x satisfies ω_n(x)∑_j w_j/(x−x_j)=1 and ω_n(x)∑_j y_jw_j/(x−x_j)=I_n y(x). The denominator sum is nonzero, giving the barycentric quotient. At a node, I_n y(x_i)=y_i separately.

For m≥1 and the evaluation p of a formal polynomial of degree at most m, or the zero polynomial, pad its coefficient vector through index m. Then p^{(m)}(x)=a_m m!_ℝ for every real x; this is zero below degree m and m!_ℝ for a monic polynomial of degree m.
For m∈ℕ, m≥6, nodes x_k=−1+k/m for 0≤k≤2m, and x_*=−1+1/(2m), the cardinal function at x_m=0 satisfies |ℓ_m(x_*)|≥9m/1280.
